impacted.role: _item_count (line 98) json.loads a whole body; the api.request logging middleware (line 113) buffers list responses with body += chunk and rebuilds them; get_content, the /api/entries handler (line 879), builds every item dict and returns the whole envelope
get_content_list (line 944), the one bounded SQL read the handler uses, returns a list
get_storage (line 221), the yield dependency that opens and closes the Storage for a request

constraints.text: Measured 2026-10-10 on a copy of cerebro's database through the app with TestClient: full 10,000-item request 2,954 MB peak RSS for a 265.7 MB body; view=list 642 MB for 15.1 MB; full with the logging middleware removed 2,176 MB.

cerebro's observability log shows GET /api/entries?limit=10000 (no view) from 172.30.100.27, the UniFi gateway address every routed client appears as, at 2026-10-10T18:26:30Z, during the run whose systemd memory peak was 2.9 GB.

FastAPI 0.142.3's request_response wraps 'await response(scope, receive, send)' inside the request-scope AsyncExitStack (fastapi/routing.py), so a request-scoped yield dependency like get_storage stays open while a StreamingResponse is sent.
Principle VIII: the API changes additively; the streamed body must keep the envelope and every field old and new clients read.
Streaming bounds memory only if rows come from a cursor rather than a pre-built list, so storage needs an iterating read beside get_content_list sharing its SQL.
